manual_rubric: Temperature, cutoff criterion and empirical-model uncertainty precede a material-quality claim; one residual does not identify gradients.
x is dimensionless; dEg/dx therefore has eV units; coefficient/model and temperature uncertainties excluded.
Positive slope in this bracket is empirical, not a universal semiconductor law.
Four-terminal voltage-probe geometry and current uniformity must be checked.
First-order, independent Gaussian errors; correlated errors require covariance.
Single carrier, low-field Hall model; polarity and offset correction explicit.
Mobility squared weights Hall signal; single-carrier density inference is invalid.
Neglecting holes increases inferred resistance here; density and mobility assumptions are supplied.
Active voltage, uniform field and ohmic reinjection; heating and velocity saturation can invalidate gain scaling.
Generation efficiency, electrical gain and EQE are different; lifetime also needs transit/model information.
Hz-to-radians factor 2*pi mandatory; pole does not uniquely identify microscopic mechanism.
Uncorrelated classical Johnson sources; source temperatures remain distinct.
Background noise contributes although useful modulation is separate; no double-counting amplifier or diode sources.
Factor sqrt2 for ASD, not factor2; negative frequencies must not be integrated again.
Finite lower limit essential for ideal 1/f; real filter changes weighting.
PSD amplitude is independently inferred, not inferred from mean current; phenomenological trap time.
Correlated processes require cross-spectra; RMS values do not add linearly.
Use transfer squared and stated pole count; one-sided post-demodulator input convention.
Poles cascade; magnitude-squared transfer functions multiply.
No spectrum is assumed outside the stated support; integration convention matters.
State difference, DC mean and sinusoidal RMS are distinct; lock-in calibration must match the chosen convention.
A/W multiplied by Ohm gives V/W; a dimensionless voltage divider alone does not.
Larger collecting area and normalized Dstar are separate metrics; matching frequency/bias/temperature required.
Changing cable C can move readout pole while intrinsic lifetime remains fixed.
Single-pole model is inconsistent; source timing, phase offset and multiple poles compete.
Bandpass, projected throughput, emissivity and response weighting still required.
Projected solid angle already contains cosine; no second pi factor; uniform source radiance and flat transmission assumed.
Cone definition supplied; actual pupil/etendue and vignetting may differ.
Two-channel spectral calibration and same emissivity are assumptions; one unknown emissivity per wavelength makes temperature non-identifiable.
Transmission and QE are separate; projected geometry and uniform band assumptions stated.
Absorption is not collection; exponential collection model is supplied, not a universal device law.
Reflection factor cancels only if common; no claim that C determines refractive index uniquely.
External versus internal QE and electrical gain assumptions explicit.
Bias supplies electrical gain energy; efficiency and gain estimates remain model dependent.
Calibration covariance and nonlinear/model uncertainty omitted.
Statistics and Hall factor are model assumptions; precision is not validation of a single-carrier model.
Apparent Arrhenius energy/prefactor over two points is not a unique mechanism assignment.
Contact inference conditional on common geometry/material; parallel surface leakage/current crowding can violate linear model.
Readout change suffices; no carrier-gain improvement follows without independent optical/current and noise controls.
Lifetime independent; optical area differs from electrical cross-section; low-field gain/contact/bias conventions explicit.
Shot/GR/1f/background omitted, so this is a restricted ideal noise budget; do not claim achieved sensitivity.

limitations: Structured quantities only; correct numbers do not establish correct physics or derivation.
